messages:
Jing: quick heads-up — canary for the priority-queue heuristics is showing increased p95 on the "analysis-heavy" route (~+30% vs baseline). Noticed CPU spikes coinciding with kernel handoffs. Posting quick traces.

Alex: can you paste the flame / perf snippet?

Jing: ```
perf top -p 1234
# top functions:
kernel_A_execute  42.1%
kernel_B_dispatch 25.3%
kv_cache_lookup    8.9%

# kv stats from runtime metrics:
kv_hits=0.72 kv_misses=0.28
microbatch_size_p50=4 microbatch_size_p95=1
``` 

Maria: that kv_miss jump smells like our token-slicing change earlier this week (512->256). Smaller chunks = more prefix variability = lower cache reuse. More kernel switches -> less stable microbatching.

Sam: agree. If kernel selection toggles mid-request we get CPU thrash + failed batching formation -> p95 up. Proposal: two quick canary experiments:
A) revert token-slicing to 512 for the route
B) reduce dynamic token budget target per-request from 200 -> 160 to encourage aggregation
Run both for 2h and compare p95 + kv_hit.

Taylor: I can run those. Plan:
- canary1 (chunking=512) -> infra/gpu-pool-7
- canary2 (budget=160) -> infra/gpu-pool-8
Success criteria: p95 delta <= +5% & kv_hit >= 0.7. Anything else?

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary1 (chunking=512) -> infra/gpu-pool-7, canary2 (budget=160) -> infra/gpu-pool-8 :rocket:

Alex: also enable kernel-selection debug for 30m: --ks-log=1 so we can see A->B handoffs. If both fail, rollback the priority-queue heuristic. Sam/Taylor, drop the short graphs back here.

Jing: ack. I'll monitor dashboards and CI traces. If p95 doesn't return to within +5% of baseline in 3h we rollback. Thanks :thumbsup:
